text.title: Mushroom murderer Erin Patterson launches last-ditch High Court appeal
text.body_text: Australia's mushroom killer Erin Patterson has launched a final legal bid to overturn her murder convictions and avoid dying in jail. Patterson, 52, was last year found guilty of murdering three relatives and attempting to kill another when she served them a toxic mushroom-laced meal in 2023.
text.summary: Erin Patterson is serving life in prison for poisoning her relatives with a toxic mushroom lunch in 2023.
text.alt_text: Mushroom murderer Erin Patterson launches last-ditch High Court appeal — BBC News - World

audio.title: Thanksgiving Storm Aftermath, Black Friday Economy, Eisenkot's Coalition Talks
audio.description: Powerful storms left nearly a million customers without power on Thanksgiving and disrupted travel across much of the country, but conditions are expected to improve heading into the weekend. Americans are expected to spend a record amount this holiday season, even as inflation forces many shoppers to cut back on other expenses to afford gifts. Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot could unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as early as next week, but divisions among his potential coalition partners could make it difficult to keep a new government together.

text.title: Way of the Warrior Kid review - Chris Pratt’s family film is as subtle as a military recruitment video
text.body_text: It’s hard to avoid the reports that boys and young men are in trouble. Across the US and UK, they’re outpaced by girls on reading tests, are more likely to have behavioral difficulties and exposed to impossible body image standards by the manosphere.
text.summary: Apple’s tone-deaf Karate Kid knock-off feels like a Maga-approved after-school special It’s hard to avoid the reports that boys and young men are in trouble . Across the US and UK, they’re outpaced by girls on reading tests, are more likely to have behavioral difficulties and exposed to impossible body image standards by the manosphere. You might think that all of this would make you think extra carefully about a film that centers on a 13-year-old boy. Not in the case of Way of the Warrior Kid, a cliche-ridden celebration of machismo and the military that greets the current climate with a shrug. At times, I had to remind myself that I wasn’t watching a Maga-funded after-school special.

audio.title: The crime-solving surgeon who inspired Sherlock Holmes
audio.description: Sherlock Holmes is one of history's greatest fictional detectives – but his powers of deduction weren't a simple figment of the imagination. In this episode, historian Lindsey Fitzharris introduces listeners to Edinburgh surgeon Joseph Bell, a medical man who used his remarkable powers of observation to diagnose patients, help pioneer modern forensic science… and investigate suspicious deaths.
